name: Sprocket
text: Run a blind 5% rollout of the new feed to users who opt into experiments. This tests the change without tipping off users, so we see real behavior, not placebo effects. The trade-off is a small group gets a different experience, but the data is cleaner than a visible A/B test. If the metric moves positively, we scale it up; if not, we kill it without noise.

name: Gauge
text: Blind rollouts hide the fact that users in the small group may not represent the broader user base. If these users self-select into the experiment, their behavior might not reflect the general population, leading to misleading data. Instead, consider a visible A/B test with a larger, randomized sample to capture diverse user reactions and ensure that any insights are widely applicable. To settle the argument, we could analyze historical data to assess user variability and the impacts of previous rollout methods.

name: Sprocket
text:
Run a visible A/B test with 5% of all users, randomized by the system, not self-selected. This gives us a clean sample that matches the broader population, so the data reflects real behavior without bias from experiment-seekers. The trade-off is that users see the change, which could introduce placebo effects or complaints, but the risk is smaller than trusting a skewed sample from a blind rollout.

name: Gauge
text: The visible A/B test still risks users altering their behavior because they know they're part of an experiment, even if they're randomized in. A better alternative might be to use a hybrid approach, where a subset of the test group is blinded to the experiment, to compare the behaviors of aware vs. unaware users. This would help settle the argument by quantifying the impact of user awareness on the experiment's validity.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run a hybrid 5% pilot with 3% visible A/B test and 2% blind rollout for one week to measure both biased and unbiased engagement, the result must deliver a comparison of user behavior with and without knowledge of the experiment, and Gauge owns the artifact by end of week.
